correctness.rationale: PASS: The exact finite first-path probability is a_(n,k)=q(1-q)^k∏_(r=1)^k (n-r)/(n-1), summing over distinct successful ancestry lengths. Conditional on a first successful path of s vertices, the second path has an exact backward recursion incorporating hits to the known successful set, newly encountered direct voters and collisions with previously exposed outside delegators. For k,s of order sqrt(n), logarithmic expansion of the no-collision product yields exp(-ct-t²/2) and the two-path success function H_c(t)=(c+t)I(c+t). Gaussian product tails justify dominated Riemann-sum convergence to P(c)=cI(c) and J(c)=∫ ce^(-ct-t²/2)H_c(t)dt. The variance is J(c)-P(c)^2=∫ce^(-ct-t²/2)(H_c(t)-P(c))dt, strictly positive because H_c is strictly increasing and equals P(c) at t=0. Monotone coupling as q rises and Markov bounds yield off-critical concentration to 0 or 1. Independently quadrature-checked P(1)=0.655679542418798472 and variance V(1)=0.0700843376534750558; these numerics corroborate, not prove, the limiting theorem.
